# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 69 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 69 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_069_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 69 constitutes Similitude 7 in its entirety — a brief but doctrinally dense chapter on the limits and conditions of repentance (*metanoia*). This chapter is one of the most cited in early Christian discussions of post-baptismal sin.

The key theological statement is in 69:3: there is no repentance beyond baptism — yet Hermas immediately qualifies this. The apparent contradiction is resolved in 69:4: the "no repentance" rule applies to those who have never sinned after baptism, or who are about to believe. For those already called who subsequently sinned, one further repentance remains available — but it is singular and final.

The phrase *haplē estin* ("it is one/singular") in 69:4 is the doctrinal crux. EMET preserves "once only," LOGOS uses "once and final," PNEUMA uses "once only and final." SOPHIA adopts "once only and final" as the fullest rendering.

The term *dipsychos* ("double-minded") appears in 69:1 as a condition that nullifies repentance's benefit — those who repent but remain double-minded about the commandments do not receive healing. All three agents render this "double-minded" consistently.

The word *katharoi* ("pure/clean") in 69:3 describes the state after baptismal forgiveness. EMET has "in purity," LOGOS "in purity," PNEUMA "in purity" — consensus holds.

All three agents agree substantially. The main divergence is EMET's more compressed phrasing vs. PNEUMA's expansive conversational style.

---

## Similitude 7 — Who Can Repent and Be Saved?

**69:1** After I had seen all these things I asked him: "Lord, I still wish to ask one more question." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "when people repent — does their repentance benefit them? Does it give them life before the Lord?" "Those who repent with their whole heart," he said, "and who cleanse themselves from all the evil things I described, and who do not add more sins to their previous ones — they receive healing from their former sins, provided they do not become double-minded concerning the commandments. And they will live for God."

**69:2** "But what about those who do not repent, but who abandon themselves to their own desires?" I said. "Do they live for God?" "They do not live for God," he said.

**69:3** "Lord," I said, "I have heard from some teachers that there is no repentance beyond the one that takes place when we go down into the water and receive forgiveness of our former sins." He said to me: "You have heard correctly. That is indeed how it stands. For the one who has received forgiveness of sins ought to sin no more, but to live in purity. But since you ask me about everything in detail, I will make this plain to you also — not to give excuse to those who will believe or to those who have already believed in the Lord."

**69:4** "For those who have already believed, or who will come to believe, have no repentance of sins — they have forgiveness of their former sins. But for those who were called before these days and sinned — for them repentance is possible. But it is once only and final. If someone sins again and again repents, it does not profit a person who lives in this way — for such a one will have difficulty living."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
